claims.claim: The Ford Model T Runabout's price started at $825 and had been lowered to $260 by 1925.
claims.episode_span: In 1908 a new Model T left the factory priced near $850. By the mid-1920s the same basic car sold for roughly $260.
claims.supporting_quote: the cost of the Runabout started at $825 (equivalent to $29,560 in 2025) . By 1925 it had been lowered to $260 (equivalent to $4,770 in 2025) .

claims.claim: Moving-line production cut Model T production time from about 12.5 hours to 93 minutes by 1914.
claims.episode_span: Early experiments showed assembly time falling from roughly twelve hours per car to a few hours; later refinements pushed it lower still.
claims.supporting_quote: reducing production time from 12 + 1 ⁄ 2 hours before to 93 minutes by 1914, while using less manpower.

claims.claim: Ford's 1914 five-dollar daily wage was aimed at reducing the heavy labor turnover that had some departments hiring 300 men a year to fill 100 slots.
claims.episode_span: the pace and monotony of the line produced high turnover until Ford countered with the famous five-dollar day
claims.supporting_quote: designed to improve the lot of his workers and especially to reduce the heavy turnover that had many departments hiring 300 men per year to fill 100 slots. Efficiency meant hiring and keeping the best workers. [ 35 ] Ford astonished the world in 1914 by offering a $5 daily wage

claims.claim: Ford vertically integrated, building or acquiring blast furnaces, a glass plant, coal mines, rubber plantations, and other upstream facilities to keep reducing Model T costs.
claims.episode_span: By owning the steel mill, the glass plant, and the rubber plantations, he removed the intermediate handling steps whose costs had been passed along in the finished price.
claims.supporting_quote: In its effort to keep reducing Model T costs while wages were rising, Ford continued to invest heavily in plant, property, and equipment. These facilities even included coal mines, rubber plantations, and forestry operations

claims.claim: Model T production ran from October 1908 to August 1927 — about nineteen years on one basic design.
claims.episode_span: Ford accepted that constraint and froze the Model T design for nineteen years so the process could be driven toward its physical limit.
